installationValues: The v0.2.6 chart asset installed by digest with the executor image and ptahVersion v0.14.0 the release manifest names (release-manifest.txt sha256:2f85b6ddb4ecc5d4878a9d994150bc9f4934d5034bfea00dc1af275b45117a24). Qualification labs add the profile settings of support/qualification/0.2.0.md: two manager replicas, restricted Pod Security on the release and workload namespaces, the frozen ResourceQuota, the kindnet NetworkPolicy build and support/qualification/0.2.0-monitoring.yaml. Each capacity lab keeps its effective Helm values and rendered manifest in the restricted evidence store.
operatingTargets: support/qualification/0.2.0.md sha256:7b4bdc6a02b9d46b8bcf5f3239701a85002dd3622d5d5357a648ce401420da06, support/qualification/0.2.0-coverage.md sha256:20f9513c8b8de20bd864728e080e68ece67427fdb4c7d0f81684283054467a16, support/qualification/0.2.0-monitoring.yaml sha256:464b4352a25ecb1ed41379034d056056bb3744ade566f4b1938558b3cbc8ae65. Its profile and monitoring files are those of revision 48; its coverage file adds the PostgreSQL extension drift scenario (#678) and the monitoring deployment check as PA-09 evidence (#675). Revisions 55 and 56 change no profile file: 55 adds the ConfigMap source scenarios after the release commit (#702), and 56 adds the v0.2.6 catalog row.
recoveryObjectives: Predeclared operator-state and database RPO: 5 minutes each. Operator-state-only loss RTO: 15 minutes with the database available. Database or combined-loss RTO: 30 minutes through application-service restoration, including manual work and verification. Procedure and timing boundaries: support/qualification/0.2.0.md.
runEvidence: Release transaction 39749825299 from bc874159 (tag v0.2.6), published by run 39913965717 and re-verified from the tag by 39913965329. Manifest-backed acceptance matrix on the release's own digests from the release source: amd64 CI 39753549451 and arm64 CI 39753553357, 54 of 54 cells and every declared scenario in its phase window. Installation from the published guide: 39916358113 (fresh on amd64), 39916364664 (fresh on arm64), 39923890536 (over v0.2.5 on amd64), 39923893894 (over v0.2.5 on arm64); the first upgrade runs, 39916361220 and 39916367748, were refused by a probe that required the predecessor's execution epoch although the executor moved, fixed in #706. Demonstration on the release digests: 39753556902. Capacity, recovery and the evidence bundles: see PA-07, PA-08 and PA-12.

PA-01.evidence: Release manifest sha256:2f85b6ddb4ecc5d4878a9d994150bc9f4934d5034bfea00dc1af275b45117a24 names every digest above; the coverage table below is the 54-cell matrix CI 39753549451 (linux/amd64) and 39753553357 (linux/arm64) ran on those digests, attempt 1, with each job ID and log hash in functional/<arch>/coverage-audit.json of the public bundle.

PA-02.evidence: Every approval-binding and drift refusal refused with zero unauthorized statements received by the database server, each with a positive control, and each fresh approval executed, on both engines and families in all 54 cells of CI 39753549451 and 39753553357 (data-plane, schema-approvals, schema-faults, migration-authority and both migration suites).

PA-03.evidence: Faults before Job creation, after dispatch, during SQL, after SQL before persistence and during lock release, with process, leader and node loss, deletion, suspension and changed bindings, showed no overlap or replay in all 54 cells of CI 39753549451 and 39753553357; the three capacity soaks repeated an all-manager restart burst on both engines without a lost or replayed operation.

PA-04.evidence: Functional refusal, retry and hung-result rows passed in CI 39753549451 and 39753553357. Each of the three capacity soaks converged after cold start, every churn round, the registry outage, the all-manager replacement and the 30-second database delay within their frozen targets; overload at 40 resources recovered after returning to 20 within 5 minutes (amd64 1.35 PostgreSQL 2m22s, arm64 1.35 PostgreSQL 1m49s, arm64 1.37 MySQL 2m44s).

PA-05.evidence: Boundary-value API cases, the installed RBAC and admission identities, the documented reader Roles, credential scans and the egress example enforced by the CNI passed in CI 39753549451 and 39753553357. Every capacity lab ran restricted Pod Security, the frozen ResourceQuota and the kindnet NetworkPolicy build, checked by the lab preflight.

PA-06.evidence: Install, upgrade, late-failure recovery, rollback refusal, uninstall, reinstall over retained CRDs and the quota- and Pod Security-constrained exported-chart install passed on 1.35, 1.36 and 1.37 on both architectures. The published guide installed v0.2.6 fresh and as an upgrade over the published v0.2.5 on both architectures: 39916358113 (fresh on amd64), 39916364664 (fresh on arm64), 39923890536 (over v0.2.5 on amd64), 39923893894 (over v0.2.5 on arm64). The upgrade moved the executor from Ptah v0.13.0 to v0.14.0; the schema stayed in sync for its applied record under the new execution epoch, with no new plan.

PA-07.evidence: The nine owner-approved recovery cells ran on the published v0.2.6 in Recovery cells runs 39916446006 and 39929447531, one job per cell on Kubernetes 1.37: operator-state, database and combined loss, each idle, during Apply and with a backup behind the database, engine and family rotating. The first run failed the two schema cells during Apply in the probe, which did not read the comment lines Ptah v0.14.0 sends before a DDL and so never found the blocked Apply; #708 fixed the probe and the second run, from the tag with only that change, ran them again. All nine passed with 698 checks, every one within its objectives: recovery 110 to 612 seconds against 900 or 1,800, database RPO bound 58 seconds or less, functional restore and cleanup passing. Records: recovery/ in the public bundle; the complete evidence, age-encrypted on the runner, is in the restricted store.

PA-08.evidence: Soak, backlog and overload passed every driver check at the support window's edges: 1.35 PostgreSQL on amd64 and arm64, 1.37 MySQL on arm64. Exact manager API demand from Metadata audit on all three API servers, complete for every manager process, peaks inside the measured windows at amd64 1.35 PostgreSQL 6,342, arm64 1.35 PostgreSQL 6,288, arm64 1.37 MySQL 6,361 for the soaks and amd64 1.35 PostgreSQL 5,804, arm64 1.35 PostgreSQL 5,722, arm64 1.37 MySQL 5,721 for the backlogs, requests per 60 seconds against 7,000. After each measurement the audit tool restored the three API servers one at a time; the busiest 60 seconds reaching into that restart period was 5,532 across all nine cells, where 0.2.3 had sent 7,131 (#657, paced by #691). Overload is outside the profile and judged by refusal, safety and recovery.

PA-09.evidence: Every alert row fired and resolved at the receiver within its frozen target, with ordinary approval waits kept from paging, in the lifecycle, alerting-operations and certificates cells of CI 39753549451 and 39753553357. The monitoring deployment check installed the published v0.2.6 from its guide with the profile's monitoring values beside a Prometheus Operator stack, scraped every manager through the chart's own ServiceMonitor, and delivered the lost-view alert and its resolution to a receiver, in runs 39916358113 (amd64) and 39916364664 (arm64) (#675).

PA-10.evidence: The published guide ran verbatim on fresh clusters for PostgreSQL and MySQL on both architectures, including the shipped kubectl-ptah reading the plan: 39916358113 (fresh on amd64), 39916364664 (fresh on arm64), 39923890536 (over v0.2.5 on amd64), 39923893894 (over v0.2.5 on arm64). All demonstration scenarios ran on the release digests (39753556902). The four signed kubectl-ptah assets read a real applied plan, schema and migration on measured capacity labs: darwin-amd64 (Darwin amd64 through Rosetta on Apple Silicon on the Docker host), darwin-arm64 (native Darwin arm64 on the Docker host), linux-amd64 (native Linux amd64), linux-arm64 (native Linux arm64).

PA-11.evidence: All eight published assets are byte-identical to the qualified draft; checksums, attestations naming bc874159 and the anonymous cosign signature verified after publication. The report-only scan of every shipped image and binary reached nothing in source. The executor binary, Ptah v0.14.0, keeps only the module-level GO-2026-5932, so the advisories of #610 are gone. The executor's Alpine zlib and musl findings and the operator base image's ca-certificates advisory DSA-6572-1 are not reachable in the admitted profile: both programs an operation Pod runs are static Go binaries, and no operator TLS client reads the system roots (release/scan/exposure-analysis.md). #705 moves the base image to the fixed ca-certificates.

PA-12.evidence: Public bundle: https://github.com/stokaro/ptah-operator/releases/tag/qualification-0.2.6, an immutable release whose assets were downloaded anonymously and matched their checksums. Restricted bundle: 13 age-encrypted archives on the evidence host, each read back, decrypted with the retained identity and refused to an unprivileged user (custody records under custody/ in the public bundle). This record and its decision are in the public bundle and at support/acceptance/0.2.0.json in the repository.

handoff.acceptedScope: The exact v0.2.6 artifacts named above, installed with the recorded values, under the frozen 0.2.0 profile (revision 48 targets): 20 resources, PostgreSQL 17 and MySQL 8.4 LTS, Kubernetes 1.35 to 1.37 on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
handoff.evidenceLocation: https://github.com/stokaro/ptah-operator/releases/tag/qualification-0.2.6; restricted archives under /home/buster/ptah-operator-evidence/0.2.6/qualification on the evidence host.
handoff.recoveryAccess: Restricted archives decrypt with the retained age identity held by Ptah Engineering; access to the evidence host is limited to its owner account.
handoff.reassessmentTriggers: Changes to shipped bytes, declared scope, installation authority or network settings, workload or retention limits, recovery objectives, or a relevant security finding require an applicability review and reruns of the affected evidence.
handoff.deploymentChecks: Before enabling autonomous Apply, install by the verified digests with the recorded values; verify admission, RBAC and network controls, monitoring-to-receiver delivery, backup access and one representative approved database change.
handoff.automaticOperationPolicy: Ptah Engineering enables autonomous operation only after the deployment checks, recovery access and the stated policy boundaries are verified; an unresolved Apply keeps the documented manual recovery path.
